candidates.title: Hillingdon Sports and Leisure Complex officially opened in Uxbridge
candidates.summary: The National Lottery Heritage Fund recorded the official opening of Hillingdon Sports and Leisure Complex in March 2010 after construction of a new indoor sports centre and restoration of the Grade II listed 1930s outdoor pool.
candidates.observed_change: A new public leisure complex and restored outdoor lido entered documented community use in Uxbridge.
candidates.geometry_source: Nominatim/OpenStreetMap geocode for Uxbridge Lido / Gatting Way, checked against the public venue name.
candidates.architect: FaulknerBrowns Architects; G. Percy Trentham for the original lido
candidates.source_name: The National Lottery Heritage Fund: £31m West London leisure complex opens
candidates.source_date_field: news date and timeline fields record February 2010 resident opening and March 2010 official opening; article text states official opening to all on 24 March
candidates.license_or_terms_note: Source page is cited for factual metadata only; reuse of page text or media requires review of National Lottery Heritage Fund website terms.
candidates.attribution: Facts attributed to The National Lottery Heritage Fund and Hillingdon Council as named in the source page.
candidates.transformation_method: Manual extraction of opening date, facility scope, publisher, and address-level point for candidate review.
candidates.limitations: The point is for atlas navigation, not a measured leisure-centre or lido boundary. The event records public opening and restoration status, not later management, maintenance, usage, or access changes.

candidates.title: Marshall Street Leisure Centre reopened after refurbishment
candidates.summary: Historic England's archive record documents a plaque marking the official reopening of the former Marshall Street Baths after renovation and refurbishment on 24 September 2010.
candidates.observed_change: A restored former public baths building in Soho returned to leisure-centre use after a long closure.
candidates.geometry_source: Nominatim/OpenStreetMap geocode for Marshall Street Leisure Centre, 15 Marshall Street.
candidates.architect: Alfred W. S. Cross and Kenneth M. B. Cross for the original baths; refurbishment architect not confirmed
candidates.source_name: Historic England Archive: Marshall Street Baths reopening plaque
candidates.source_date_field: archive record title and description state official reopening date
candidates.license_or_terms_note: Historic England archive record is cited for factual metadata only; reuse of images or long descriptive text requires Historic England archive terms review.
candidates.attribution: Facts attributed to Historic England Archive, Played in Britain Collection record PLA01/03/0160.
candidates.transformation_method: Manual extraction of reopening date, venue name, and site point for candidate review.
candidates.limitations: The source is an archive image record for a reopening plaque. It confirms the reopening milestone but does not provide a full project contract record, operational programme, or measured building footprint.

candidates.title: Jubilee Gardens reopened as a re-landscaped South Bank park
candidates.summary: Jubilee Gardens Trust records the 2012 re-landscaping by West 8, the transfer of management responsibility to the community-based trust in May 2012, and the later royal inauguration of the new gardens.
candidates.observed_change: A re-landscaped public park with new planting, paths, seating, and play space entered documented public use beside the London Eye.
candidates.geometry_source: Nominatim/OpenStreetMap geocode for Jubilee Gardens, South Bank.
candidates.source_date_field: history page states May 2012 trust handover for the new green space and October 2012 inauguration
candidates.license_or_terms_note: Source page is cited for factual metadata only; reuse of text, images, or trust materials requires review of Jubilee Gardens Trust terms.
candidates.attribution: Facts attributed to Jubilee Gardens Trust.
candidates.transformation_method: Manual extraction of re-landscaping year, management handover month, designer, and park point for candidate review.
candidates.limitations: The event uses May 2012 for the documented management handover of the new green space; the separate royal inauguration is recorded by the source as October 2012. The coordinate is a park navigation point, not a measured landscape boundary.

candidates.title: Leicester Square reopened after public-realm transformation
candidates.summary: The Greater London Authority recorded Leicester Square officially reopening on 23 May 2012 after a 17-month public-realm transformation managed by Westminster City Council.
candidates.observed_change: Leicester Square's public realm reopened with new paving, planting, lighting, seating, and works around the central Shakespeare statue.
candidates.source_name: London City Hall: Leicester Square reopening press release
candidates.publisher: Greater London Authority / London City Hall
candidates.source_date_field: created date and article text state official reopening evening on 23 May 2012
candidates.license_or_terms_note: Source page is cited for factual metadata only; reuse of page text or media requires review of London City Hall terms.
candidates.attribution: Facts attributed to Greater London Authority / London City Hall and Westminster City Council as named in the source page.
candidates.transformation_method: Manual extraction of reopening date, scope, project partners, and square point for candidate review.
candidates.limitations: The event records the square reopening milestone. It does not separate individual paving, lighting, planting, fountain, cinema, or adjoining private-investment works.

candidates.title: The Blue Market Place reopened after transformation
candidates.summary: Southwark Council invited residents to a 31 July 2021 celebration for the new and improved Market Place at The Blue after community-led public-realm and market improvements.
candidates.observed_change: The Blue Market Place in Bermondsey reopened with a redefined market square, new seating, trees, lighting, stall layout, artwork, and a clock tower.
candidates.geometry_source: Nominatim/OpenStreetMap geocode for The Blue Market, Market Place, Bermondsey.
candidates.source_name: Southwark Council: Feeling Blue? Join celebration at Bermondsey town centre following marketplace transformation
candidates.source_date_field: news page dated 26 July 2021 states celebration and reopening on Saturday 31 July
candidates.license_or_terms_note: Source page is cited for factual metadata only; reuse of Southwark Council text or media requires review of council website terms.
candidates.attribution: Facts attributed to Southwark Council, The Blue BID, Community Opportunity, Big Local Works, Hayatsu Architects, and Assemble as named in the source page.
candidates.transformation_method: Manual extraction of reopening date, public-realm scope, design team, funding context, and market point for candidate review.

candidates.observed_change: The children's theatre reopened with updated theatre spaces, rehearsal and development studios, a creative learning studio, play areas, cafe, shop, and improved access.

candidates.summary: Jacksons Lane's 2022/23 annual review records a reopening celebration in April 2022 after a two-year closure and £4.6 million redevelopment of the Grade II listed arts centre.
candidates.observed_change: The arts centre reopened with reworked accessibility, studio, foyer, cafe-bar, theatre, backstage, and public-area facilities.

candidates.source_date_field: annual review states reopening was celebrated in April 2022 after a two-year closure; venue history page states works completed in March 2022

candidates.attribution: Facts attributed to Jacksons Lane Annual Review 2022/23.
